description_full: Nature's Sunshine Products, Inc., a natural health and wellness company, manufactures and sells nutritional and personal care products in Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, and internationally. The company distributes general health products related to blood sugar support, bone health, cellular health, cognitive function, joint health, mood, sexual health, sleep, sports and energy, and vision; and immune products to support and strengthen the human immune system. It also offers cardiovascular products; digestive products to regulate intestinal and digestive functions; personal care products for external use, including oils and lotions, aloe vera gel, herbal shampoo, herbal skin treatment, toothpaste, and skin cleanser. In addition, the company provides weight management products, such as meal replacements and products that increase caloric burn rate. It offers its products under the Nature's Sunshine and Synergy Worldwide brands through its network of independent consultants to customers. Nature's Sunshine Products, Inc. was founded in 1972 and is headquartered in Lehi, Utah.

financial_summary: Nature's Sunshine Products, Inc is a micro-cap consumer defensive business with a $188M market cap on $480M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 20% against a 8% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 74% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $29M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.81× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 8.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.5% of the shares.
